checks.primaryClaim: 90-120 days. FGD record (Mode B, no ED): 'Obtaining a fresh factory license, from initial building-plan preparation to final approval, takes 3 months on average, driven substantially by rejection cycles during scrutiny and the need to sequence approvals across multiple departments.' Participant quote: 'If you have everything in hand, then you fill in the application, three months, four months it takes.'
checks.sourceSays: The Factories & Boilers Department's own statutory Right-to-Service notification (issued under section 3 of the Kerala State Right to Service Act, 2012) fixes the service delivery time limit (column 4, 'സേവനം ലഭ്യമാകുന്ന സമയപരിധി') for Sl. No. 3, 'രജിസ്ട്രേഷനും ലൈസൻസ് അനുവദിക്കലും' (Registration and grant of Licence — the fresh Factory Licence, applied for in Form No. 2, for both section 85 and section 2(m) factories) at '20 ദിവസം' = 20 days. The antecedent step, Sl. No. 1 'പെർമിറ്റ് അനുവദിക്കൽ/ഭേദഗതി' (grant/amendment of Permit — approval of site, building plans and machinery layout in Form No. 1 under Rule 3) is fixed at '30 ദിവസം' = 30 days. The two departmental steps therefore carry a notified statutory ceiling of 50 days in total, against the 90-120 days reported by businesses. Related rows for completeness: permit revalidation 15 days (Sl. 2), licence renewal 15 days (Sl. 4), licence amendment 15 days (Sl. 5), licence transfer 15 days (Sl. 6). The notification is signed by the Director of Factories & Boilers and its explanatory note records that it supersedes the department's earlier RTS notification published in Kerala Gazette No. 29, Volume 12, dated 18/07/2023.

The FGD captured only ₹25,000-30,000 per load for hazardous waste disposal and ₹60,000-70,000 for licensed engineer/agency charges.
checks.sourceSays: The statutory fee schedule was found and read. S.R.O. No. 16/2025 (G.O.(P) No.1/2025/LBR dated 4 January 2025), made under section 112 of the Factories Act, 1948, substitutes a new APPENDIX - I [See Rule 5(1)] of the Kerala Factories Rules, 1957 — the Factory Licence fee itself. It is a matrix of total installed power (kilowatt) against 'Maximum number of persons to be employed in any day during the year'. Worked values: Nil power / up to 9 workers = Rs. 385; Nil power / up to 50 workers = Rs. 1,340; Up to 10 kW / up to 20 workers = Rs. 1,340; Up to 50 kW / up to 100 workers = Rs. 5,549; Up to 100 kW / up to 200 workers = Rs. 15,853; Up to 500 kW / up to 500 workers = Rs. 49,576; rising to Rs. 510,324 for above 500,000 kW with above 3,000 workers. Note (1): 'All remittance shall be as per this schedule with effect from the date of publication of notification.' Note (2): '1 HP = 0.746 KW.' The same notification substitutes APPENDIX - III, 'SCHEDULE OF FEES PRESCRIBED UNDER THE KERALA FACTORIES RULES, 1957 OTHER THAN THE FEES PRESCRIBED IN APPENDIX I', which prices the permit/plan-approval stage: 'Approval of plan for construction, modification, extension etc. of factory building including layout of machinery and grant of permit thereof first time scrutiny' (Rule 3) = 'Rs. 196/- per every 10 sq.m of plinth area or part thereof subject to a minimum Rs. 1904/- for each application'; the same for 'second and subsequent scrutinise revision after total rejection' = 'Rs. 1904/- for each application'; 'Revalidation of permit issued under Rule 3' = 'Fee originally paid for the last permit'; 'Amendment of licence' (Rule 6(4)) = 'Rs. 955/- for each amendment'; 'Transfer of licence' (Rule 8(3)) = '25% of license fee in case of transfer of license in favour of legal heirs. 100% of license fee for other transfers.' Recognition of a Draftsman-A/B/C (Rule 3(2)(b)(iii)) = Rs. 5,750 / Rs. 3,450 / Rs. 1,725 per application. The explanatory note records that these rates were last revised by G.O.(P) No.72/2022/LBR dated 13 July 2022 (S.R.O. No. 722/2022), so the January 2025 rates are the current ones. The RTS notification independently confirms the payment route: licence fee 'KFR 1957 Appendix – I- പ്രകാരം' (as per Appendix I) under 'അക്കൗണ്ട് ഹെഡ് നമ്പർ 0230-00-104' paid 'ഓൺലൈനായി' (online).

checks.primaryClaim: No deemed approval. FGD record: 'Standard Factory and Boilers licenses do not have operational deemed approval, per participants.' (status: 'no', days: null)
checks.sourceSays: The Kerala Factories Rules, 1957 contain no deemed-approval provision for the grant of a factory licence, and instead positively require an actually granted licence before operation. Rule 5(3): 'No manufacturing process shall be carried on in any factory without a licence having been granted by the Chief Inspector or the Deputy Chief Inspector and is in force for the time being.' Rule 5(1) makes the grant discretionary and conditional ('A licence for a factory may be granted by the Chief Inspector or the Deputy Chief Inspector in Form No.4, on an application made in the prescribed Form No. 2 and on payment of the fees specified in Appendix I'), with an express power to refuse registration and grant. Equivalently at the permit stage, Rule 3(1): 'No site shall be used for the location of a factory nor shall any building be constructed, reconstructed or extended for use as a factory... unless the previous permission in writing is obtained', and Rule 3(6) preserves a power to refuse. The remedy the State actually provides for delay is appellate, not deemed approval: the RTS notification's columns 6 and 7 designate, for Sl. No. 3 (Registration and grant of Licence), a First Appellate Authority (ഡയറക്ടർ ഓഫ് ഫാക്ടറീസ് & ബോയിലേഴ്സ്, Director of Factories & Boilers) and a Second Appellate Authority (ഗവൺമെന്റ് സെക്രട്ടറി, തൊഴിലും നൈപുണ്യവും (ബി) വകുപ്പ്, Government Secretary, Labour and Skills (B) Department).

checks.primaryClaim: FGD record lists only four generic items — 'Blueprint building plans', 'Structural integrity certificates', 'Land deeds', 'Local body permits' — with the note that it is an 'FGD-only record, not yet verified against an official ED' and that documents 'must reportedly be repeatedly uploaded or submitted separately across KSPCB, Local Panchayat, Fire & Safety, and FAB Kerala'. No official checklist was captured.
checks.sourceSays: The official, itemised checklist exists in two published sources and is far more specific than the FGD list. (A) PERMIT stage — RTS notification Sl. No. 1, column 3, and Kerala Factories Rules 1957 Rule 3(2): application in Form No. 1; a flow chart of the manufacturing process with a brief description of its various stages; the scrutiny/inspection fee under account head 0230-00-104 paid online; a site plan drawn to a scale of 1:400 showing the factory site and all factory buildings together with adjacent roads, drains and other buildings, plus site plans within a 100 metre radius, certified by the applicant and a recognised draftsman with digital signature; plan, elevation and cross-sections of the various buildings with full particulars of natural lighting, ventilation and means of escape in case of fire or accident, similarly certified; a machinery layout recording the machines and motors to be installed with horsepower noted separately, similarly certified; details of the rainwater harvesting system and artificial groundwater recharge system marked on the plan; for factories carrying on hazardous or environmentally polluting manufacturing processes, a No Objection Certificate from the Kerala State Pollution Control Board and a certificate approving the factory location from the Government Town Planner; and for Major Accident Hazard (MAH) factories, a copy of the Government order granting permission under section 41A. (B) REGISTRATION AND LICENCE stage — RTS notification Sl. No. 3, column 3: application in Form No. 2; the licence fee as per KFR 1957 Appendix I under account head 0230-00-104 paid online; a Stability Certificate in Form No. 3 (for section 2(m) factories only); documents proving ownership of the factory — partnership deed / Memorandum & Articles of Association / society bye-laws, with list of directors or partners; documents of the appointment of the factory occupier (Director / Managing Director / Managing Partner / Chairman / President); the current year's land tax receipt for the property on which the factory stands; the rent agreement where the factory building is rented; a power of attorney where the occupier is absent; and the KSPCB NOC plus Town Planner location-approval certificate for hazardous and polluting factories. The department FAQ adds the fire-safety plan explicitly: 'The plans of fire layouts with legends of firefighting equipment clearly indicating the position and distribution of various fire protection and preventive measures in various buildings as well as in factory site with means of escape on fires.' The FAQ also fixes who may draw them: 'The plans prepared for the purpose of Factory Permit shall be only prepared by the Department Approved Draftsman. All the plans shall be certified and signed by the Department Approved Draftsman as well as by the Factory occupier.' Rule 3(2)(b) states the same requirement in rule form: plans 'shall be prepared by a person not below the rank of a draughtsman recognized by the Chief Inspector or the Deputy Chief Inspector/ State Government'.

checks.primaryClaim: FGD record: automationLevel 'partial', applicantOfficeVisit 'yes', portal recorded as 'K-SWIFT single-window platform (concept referenced; physical inter-department coordination still reported as necessary)' with url null. Five steps: engage licensed engineer for plans; submit application and plans across departments; administrative scrutiny of blueprints (frequently rejected up to 3 times); joint departmental inspection; final approval. Gap flag VAGUE: 'The process is described only in general terms ("relatively straightforward"); no step-level timeline breakdown is given.'
checks.sourceSays: The official sources identify the actual channel (which the FGD left as null) and state the process is to be transacted online. The RTS notification's headnote above the service table reads: 'ക്രമ നമ്പർ 1 മുതൽ 26 വരെയുള്ള സേവനങ്ങൾ ലഭ്യമാകുന്നതിന് ഓൺലൈനായി അപേക്ഷ സമർപ്പിക്കുകയും ഫീസ് ഒടുക്കുകയും ചെയ്യേണ്ടതാണ്. അപേക്ഷയോടൊപ്പം സമർപ്പിക്കേണ്ട പ്രമാണങ്ങൾ pdf ഫോർമാറ്റിലും ഫോട്ടോ jpg ഫോർമാറ്റിലും അപ് ലോഡ് ചെയ്യേണ്ടതാണ്' — i.e. for services at serial numbers 1 to 26 (which include the Permit at Sl. 1 and Registration and grant of Licence at Sl. 3) the application must be submitted online and the fee paid online, and the documents accompanying the application must be uploaded in PDF format and photographs in JPG format. The department's own portal, not K-SWIFT, is named as the filing channel: FAQ on Registration, Q5 'How to apply for factory registration?' — 'Visit the website www.fabkerala.gov.in and register the occupier using new registration link. Then enter factory details, Form 2 clearly and correctly and upload required documents and pay fee online and submit the application.' FAQ on Permit, Q2 — 'The User shall take One Time Registration through the Official Website of Department(www.fab.kerala.gov.in) and apply online for the Permit approval along with mandatory documents'. The official sequence is also fixed, and is two statutory stages, not one: FAQ on Permit, Q1 — 'Any of the Industries employing More than 10 Numbers of Workers requires to get the factory permit approval before applying for the registration. Factories employing less than 10 workers shall obtain registration and license according to the notification under section 85 of Factories Act 1948.' Scope: FAQ on Registration, Q1 — 'Industries employing three or more workers and carrying out any manufacturing process specified in the Factories Act, 1948 are required to register with the department and obtain a license.' The permit is time-limited, forcing the licence stage to follow promptly: FAQ on Permit, Q5, validity 'One Year from the Date of Approval', matching Rule 3(4): 'The permission so granted will be valid for one year only unless it is revalidated, for completion of construction.' On inspection, no pre-grant inspection is prescribed in Rule 5; what the Rules require before manufacturing begins is a third-party certificate, Rule 3(7)(a): 'No manufacturing process shall be carried on in any building of a factory constructed, reconstructed or extended or taken into use as a factory... until a Certificate of Stability in Form No. 3 in respect of that building has been obtained from a Competent Person', valid for a maximum of five years. Rule 3(2) does contemplate a single-window entry point, but names KSIDC/DIC rather than K-SWIFT: the application may be made 'in the composite application form to be submitted to the Green Channel Counter of the Kerala State Industries Development Corporation or District Industries Centres or other notified agencies as the case may be, who will forward a copy of the same to the Department concerned.'

remarks: TRANSPORT CAVEAT: every fabkerala.gov.in citation above is marked "transport": "http" and was NOT transport-authenticated. Re-tested this session: the https:// variant of the same path returned HTTP 403 Forbidden (the proxy CONNECT tunnel itself established fine, so this is the origin/WAF refusing, not a network failure). Per the spec no User-Agent spoofing or other WAF workaround was attempted. The plain http:// variant served the content, and the four PDFs were independently sanity-checked with `file` (valid PDFs of 18, 5 and 126 pages) and carry genuine Kerala Gazette mastheads, Regn.No. KERBIL/2012/45073, digital-signature statements and eOffice generation footers from the Factories and Boilers department, which is corroborating but not a substitute for TLS.

MOST SIGNIFICANT FINDING — the timeline contradiction is a 50-day statutory ceiling against a 90-120 day lived experience, and the fee schedule shows one concrete mechanism for the gap. The FGD's central pain point is that 'applications are frequently rejected up to 3 times for minor technical or layout discrepancies'. Appendix III of S.R.O. No. 16/2025 prices exactly that: a first-time plan scrutiny costs Rs. 196 per 10 sq.m of plinth area (minimum Rs. 1,904), and every 'second and subsequent scrutinise revision after total rejection' costs a further flat Rs. 1,904 per application. The rejection cycle businesses describe is therefore a billable, repeat-charged event under the current notified fee rules — an independently verified corroboration of the FGD pain point that the FGD itself did not quantify.

The RTS 20-day figure is for the licence step alone (Sl. 3, Registration and grant of Licence). Because Kerala requires the Permit (Sl. 1, 30 days) to be obtained BEFORE applying for registration for factories employing more than 10 workers — stated explicitly in the department FAQ — the honest statutory comparator for a fresh factory licence is 30 + 20 = 50 days of departmental processing. This still excludes the privately-borne pre-application work the FGD counted into its 90-120 days (engaging a department-approved draftsman to prepare certified plans, at a reported Rs. 60,000-70,000) and excludes the prerequisite KSPCB NOC and Town Planner location certificate, which are other departments' timelines. Reviewers should present the 50-day figure as the State's own service-delivery commitment, not as a claim that the whole journey takes 50 days.

VERIFIED CORROBORATION OF AN FGD PAIN POINT: the FGD finding that 'small applicants cannot apply directly on their own and are forced to engage outsourced licensed engineers or agencies' is not merely a market condition — it is a legal requirement. Kerala Factories Rules Rule 3(2)(b) requires plans to be 'prepared by a person not below the rank of a draughtsman recognized by the Chief Inspector', and the department FAQ states plans 'shall be only prepared by the Department Approved Draftsman' and must be certified and signed by both that draftsman and the occupier. Appendix III of S.R.O. 16/2025 prices draftsman recognition at Rs. 5,750 (A) / Rs. 3,450 (B) / Rs. 1,725 (C) per application.

FGD PORTAL FIELD IS LIKELY MISATTRIBUTED. The FGD record names K-SWIFT as the portal (url null). Both official sources name the department's own site, www.fabkerala.gov.in, as the filing channel for the Permit and for Registration/Licence, reached via a one-time occupier registration. Kerala Factories Rules Rule 3(2) does allow a composite application through the 'Green Channel Counter of the Kerala State Industries Development Corporation or District Industries Centres or other notified agencies', which is the single-window route in the Rules — but it is named as KSIDC/DIC, not K-SWIFT. Note also that the FABOS application portal itself (idms.fabkerala.gov.in) and kswift.kerala.gov.in were both unreachable in the source-verification pass on both protocols, so the live filing system could not be independently inspected; only the published rules and notifications about it were verified.

FEE SCHEDULE CURRENCY: the Appendix I and Appendix III rates cited are from S.R.O. No. 16/2025, in force 'at once' from 4 January 2025, which replaced the prior S.R.O. No. 722/2022 rates. The notification's own explanatory note confirms the 2022 rates were the immediately preceding ones, so these are current as of this validation date and are not a superseded schedule.

DEEMED-APPROVAL NUANCE A REVIEWER SHOULD NOT MISREAD: there is no deemed approval for a FRESH licence, which is what the FGD was describing. However, the Kerala Factories Rules do contain a continuation-of-validity provision at the RENEWAL stage only — Rule 7(2): where a renewal application in Form No. 2 is made 'not less than two months before the date on which the licence expires... the premises shall be held to be duly licenced until such date as the Competent Authority... renews the licence or till the Competent Authority intimates the applicant in writing his refusal'. This is a deeming of continued licensed status pending decision, not a deemed grant, and it does not apply to FAL. It is flagged here because it would be easy to cite it mistakenly as deemed approval, and because it may be directly relevant to the separate RFAL (Renewal of Factory License) record.

SARAL KERALAM BILL — NOT CITED AS A CHECK, DELIBERATELY. The source list's verification pass read the full text of the SARAL (Simplified & Accelerated Regulatory Approvals and Licensing) Keralam Bill, 2026 (Bill No. 19, Kerala Niyamasabha) and established that its Schedule overrides only seven named local-body laws (Panchayat Raj Act 1994, Municipality Act 1994, Cinemas Regulation Act 1958, Panchayat/Municipality Building Rules 2019, and the Panchayat/Municipality 'Issue of Licence to Enterprises' Rules 2025/2026) for projects above Rs. 25 crore. The Factories Act, 1948 and the Kerala Factories Rules, 1957 are NOT scheduled, so SARAL Keralam does not currently alter the FAL timeline, fee or process, and no check above rests on it. Its schedule is amendable by notification (clause 23), so this should be re-checked in any future pass.

The department 'Know Your Services' downloads/user-guides page and the department homepage were fetched and read but yielded no additional FAL-specific facts beyond those already carried by the RTS notification, the fee notification, the Rules and the FAQ; they are listed in sourcesRead for completeness.

The numerals and the word 'ദിവസം' (days) extract cleanly, and the table structure, serial numbers, service names and English fragments ('KFR 1957 Appendix - I', account head '0230-00-104', 'Form No. 1', 'Form No. 2') were legible and cross-checked against the Kerala Factories Rules and the FAQ, which agree.
